newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end a record close in split market.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end a record close in split market.

text.p: Swiss shares ended at a record close in a split market.
The rising dollar supported the industrial sector, which took the whole market higher. Gains in banks and insurers, however, were only marginal, dealers said.
News that brokers Kleinwort Benson had raised its earnings forecast for Nestle because of the weak Swiss franc not only helped Nestle, but also supported other export-oriented shares.
"If the currency is good for Nestle then its also good for other companies", one dealer said.
The blue-chip SMI index rose 21.3 points to 3,966.2 points while the broad SPI added 12.13 points to 2,539.19.
Novartis, up 14 francs to 1,547, led the active list. Roche gained 115 francs to 10,630.
Wall Street' firm opening also supported sentiment as did Thursday's U.S. PPI data.
News Switzerland's unemployment rate reached a post-war high in December was taken as proof that Swiss interest rates would continue to stay low, supporting the stock market.
Shares in cement producer Holderbank added 20 francs to 1,004 while Alusuisse added 15 francs to 1,145.
In the insurance sector, Winterthur's registered shares stood out because they rose 13 francs to 781, while Swiss Re gained only two to 1,398.
UBS bearer shares firmed one franc to 1,180 while CS group's shares were steady at 134.50.
The second-tier sector saw Logitech almost 10 percent higher at 216 francs with Saurer and Swisslog also posting gains.
